diagnostic_evidence.quote: Beside theoretical results and justifications of our method, we present a large number of numerical examples
In other words, the conjecture is that
As a direct consequence of the UCP stated in Theorem~\ref{teo:ucp}, it is not possible to find a non-constant boundary data $g$ fulfilling~\eqref{eqn:idcond}.
The threshold $\varepsilon$ has to be chosen coherently with the value of $\lambda_n$. More details about this threshold will be given in the next sections.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction and abstract promise a main theoretical result justifying the Kernel Method. Section 4 contains no theorem; the only formal result (Lemma lem:mainl) has a hypothesis (existence of a kernel element g) that, by the paper's own Theorem teo:ucp, is never satisfied for non-constant g. No statement or proof links a small eigenvalue lambda_n to the reconstructed set tilde D approximating D: the bound int_D p <= lambda_n/k_1 does not compare with the power outside D (int_Omega p = <Lambda_bg g_n,g_n> also tends to zero for the normalized high-order eigenfunctions), and equality of int_{tilde D} p with an integral over D does not force tilde D = D (the hollow example explicitly shows tilde D != D). The justification of the algorithm rests on an explicitly labelled 'conjecture' and an 'educated guess'.

failure_location.quote: in~ Section\ref{sec:main} we state our main result and we give a first reconstruction algorithm

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword the introduction/abstract to state that Section 4 presents the method and its heuristic motivation (Lemma lem:mainl plus the eigenvalue bounds), and that no convergence/approximation theorem for tilde D is proved.
issues.overall_effect: The reconstruction guarantee of the Kernel Method (tilde D approximates D) is heuristic, not established; the prose overstates the theoretical content.
issues.title: Announced 'main result' / theoretical justification of the reconstruction does not exist in the paper
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws the promised theoretical justification of the algorithm's output, a substantive loss, but the lemma, bounds and numerical evidence survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The standard inequality has <(Lambda_{sigma_2}-Lambda_{sigma_1})g,g> in the middle (since Lambda is decreasing in sigma). With sigma_1=sigma_D<=sigma_2=sigma_bg, the inequality as printed would give <(Lambda_D-Lambda_bg)g,g> <= -int_D(sigma_bg-sigma_a)|grad u_bg|^2 <= 0, contradicting the positivity invoked two lines later and not yielding (eqn:lem1). The conclusion (eqn:lem1) is correct only under the sign-corrected inequality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace Lambda_{sigma_1}-Lambda_{sigma_2} by Lambda_{sigma_2}-Lambda_{sigma_1} in (eqn:in1); the rest of the proof then follows.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma lem:mainl as written relies on an incorrectly stated premise; the lemma itself is true once the sign is corrected. The Section 6 bounds (eqn:sogp3) are stated with the correct orientation and are not affected.
issues.title: Recalled monotonicity inequality (eqn:in1) has the operator difference with reversed sign, so (eqn:lem1) does not follow as written
issues.why_classification: A one-symbol local correction of the invoked inequality restores the inference with no loss of content.

issues.failure_explanation: No openness or positive-measure condition is imposed on A. Taking A a single point (or any null set), every solution is trivially 'constant in A', so the theorem as stated would force every solution to be constant, which is false (e.g. u = x_1 for sigma = 1). The unique continuation results cited require A to be a nonempty open set.

failure_location.quote: If $u$ is constant in $A$, then $u$ is constant in $\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require A to be a nonempty open subset of Omega (D has nonempty interior in the application).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem teo:ucp is false as stated; its use to argue that ker(Lambda_D - Lambda_bg) contains no non-constant g is valid only after requiring D (resp. A) to have nonempty interior.
issues.title: Weak UCP stated for an arbitrary subset A, which makes the statement false
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypothesis is a local routine fix that preserves the intended use.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Throughout this paper, $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, with $n\geq2$, is the region occupied by the conducting material.
where $\sigma\in L_+^{\infty}(\Omega)$ is the electrical conductivity.
with $\sigma\in L^{\infty}_+(\Omega)$ for $n=2$ or $\sigma$ Lipschitz continuous for $n=3$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's setting allows any n>=2 and sigma_bg merely in L^infty_+. The cited UCP covers only n=2 with L^infty coefficients and n=3 with Lipschitz coefficients; for n=3 with non-Lipschitz L^infty background and for n>=4 the claimed non-existence of non-constant kernel elements is unsupported (unique continuation is known to fail for merely bounded coefficients in n>=3).

failure_location.quote: As a direct consequence of the UCP stated in Theorem~\ref{teo:ucp}, it is not possible to find a non-constant boundary data $g$ fulfilling~\eqref{eqn:idcond}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to n=2 with sigma_bg in L^infty_+ and n=3 with Lipschitz sigma_bg, or add these hypotheses to the standing assumptions.
issues.overall_effect: The statement that (eqn:idcond) has no non-constant solution is established only for n=2 (L^infty) and n=3 (Lipschitz sigma_bg), not for the paper's advertised generality; the method itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Non-existence of kernel elements asserted in a regime (n>=2, L^infty background) not covered by the cited UCP
issues.why_classification: A standard scope restriction fixes the claim; nothing in the algorithm or its analysis depends on the kernel being trivial.

issues.failure_explanation: Weyl-type bounds |lambda_k(A+N)-lambda_k(A)| <= ||N|| require A+N to be self-adjoint (and, for the eigenvalues to form a decreasingly ordered sequence at all, compactness or a finite-dimensional setting). For a general bounded N, Lambda_n need not be self-adjoint (complex eigenvalues, no decreasing order) or compact (possibly no eigenvalue sequence), so the statement is ill-defined/unsupported as written. The numerical section implicitly symmetrizes the noise, confirming the missing hypothesis.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume N self-adjoint and compact (or work in the finite-dimensional matrix setting) in (eqn:noise)/Proposition prop:pert.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:pert and the noise-level reasoning built on it hold only under a self-adjointness (and compactness/finite-rank) assumption on N that is not stated.
issues.title: Eigenvalue perturbation proposition stated for an arbitrary bounded (non-self-adjoint) noise operator
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard hypothesis, which the numerical model already satisfies, restores the result with no loss.

issues.failure_explanation: From P-P_b <= int_D ((sigma_bg-sigma_a)/sigma_a) sigma_bg |grad u_bg|^2 one only gets P-P_b <= ((sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m)/sigma_a^m) int_D sigma_bg|grad u_bg|^2, i.e. the lower bound constant is sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m), not sigma_a^m/Delta_sigma with Delta_sigma=sigma_bg^m-sigma_a^M. Since Delta_sigma <= sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m, the printed bound is strictly stronger than what is derivable for non-uniform conductivities (they coincide only in the uniform case).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the lower constant by sigma_a^m/(sigma_bg^M-sigma_a^m) and adjust the alpha-interval and the remark's condition accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The admissible interval for alpha in (eqn:thr) and the condition sigma_bg^m > sigma_a^m+sigma_a^M in the following remark are not justified for non-uniform sigma_a, sigma_bg; the uniform-conductivity examples are unaffected.
issues.title: Lower bound in (eqn:sogp3) uses the wrong constant
issues.why_classification: A local recomputation of a constant with no change to the method or conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Specifically, clear bounds for admissible values of $\varepsilon$ can be analytically derived.

issues.failure_explanation: In Section 4 epsilon is defined as a threshold on the power density p(x) (tilde D = {p < epsilon}). The bounds (eqn:sogp3) constrain the integral int_D p, a power, not the pointwise density; so the deduction 'the threshold has to be chosen as epsilon = alpha lambda_n ||g_n||^2' is a non sequitur (and dimensionally inconsistent) for the density threshold. The final algorithm (eqn:thr2) instead imposes an integral condition, and the closing remark reintroduces epsilon as a density threshold tuned until (eqn:thr2) holds, so the same symbol denotes two different objects.

failure_location.quote: So the threshold has to be chosen as

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (eqn:thr) as a prescription for the target value of int_{tilde D} p (i.e. int_{tilde D} p = alpha lambda_n ||g_n||^2), and rename the density threshold used in the final remark.
issues.overall_effect: The stated 'bounds for admissible epsilon' do not apply to the density threshold of Section 4; only the integral-condition form of the algorithm is supported by (eqn:sogp3).
issues.title: Threshold (eqn:thr) derived from an integral bound is presented as a pointwise power-density threshold
issues.why_classification: The final algorithm is already in the consistent integral form; only the intermediate statement needs rewording.
